newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Perez Companc Venezuela oil output still rising.
newsitem.headline: Perez Companc Venezuela oil output still rising.

text.p: Oil production from Venezuela's Oritupano/Leona field operated by Argentina's Perez Companc reached 40,000 barrels per day (bpd) this month and is growing by 1,000 bpd per month, a company official said on Monday.
Horacio Begaries, managing director of Perez Companc Venezuela, said output should reach 50,000 bpd by March next year and the company had no fixed target for stabilising production.
In an interview with Reuters, he said Perez would invest $108 million this year in the Oritupano/Leona fields which still contain 160 million barrels in reserves.

Perez Companc operates the fields under Venezuela's 1993 operating agreements which allowed private companies to operate mature oilfields for subsidiaries of state-run Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) in exchange for a fixed fee and reimbursement of capital expenditure.

The fields within the Oritupano/Leona area produce crude with an average quality of 18-19 degrees API. The heavy Oritupano grade is transported by PDVSA subsidiary Corpoven through pipelines to its Puerto la Cruz refinery, while the lighter Leona output is shipped to the Orinoco Belt to be diluted with extra- heavy crude.
Perez Companc is also exploring for oil under a profit sharing contract with Venezuela's Corporacion Venezolana de Petroleo (CVP) in the central San Carlos block.
Begaries said the company was currently interpreting 70 kilometres of seismic data and plans to drill its first exploratory well at the end of 1997 or beginning of 1998.
The total number of wells due to be drilled depends on the results from the first two wells, Begaries said.
Investment this year in San Carlos will reach $16 million.
Under the contract signed with Perez Companc, CVP can take 40 percent of any eventual profits from this field.
